sources.locator: The nineteen skills/*/SKILL.md path names; docs/design/skill/skill.md and the public_entries contract paths; design/requirements/published-products.md retained child-obligation inventory
sources.basis: Directory-entry inspection establishes canonical source names and file existence only; published-purpose descriptions come from the current owning Designs. No SKILL.md content was read or invoked, no installed package was inspected, and no current public-release qualification or complete skill implementation audit is claimed.

proposed.choice: Map named published skills to bounded procedural contributions while retaining specialist behavior ownership and explicit unmapped detail.
proposed.rationale: Readers need to discover each public skill's purpose, applicable behavior, and current authority without treating the common guidance Module as the owner of every specialist responsibility.
alternatives: List all skills only under MOD-012 without showing distinct assurance, authority, and learning contributions; this would obscure their existing owners.
Treat every skill as a new Module or map its name mechanically to a similarly named Function; neither establishes a coherent responsibility or equivalent behavior.
consequences: The relation guides denotes an agent-facing procedure for the stated Function contribution, not a service invocation, runtime implementation, or proven conformance. Features and accountable Modules are derived from the existing Function relationships.

FUNC-050, FUNC-051, and FUNC-052 define the common capability-selection, invocation, and resource boundary across this inventory. Entry mappings emphasize the selected activity and distinguish partial common correspondence from specialist coverage; they are not exhaustive instruction or call graphs.

Current source contracts retain every detailed clause. Published Design/proposal/plan outputs and customer-project adoption remain unchanged; a mapping to common guidance does not adopt REM entity authoring.

All nineteen entries have an explicit mapping disposition, but several expose only common specialist guidance. Their linked specialist procedures require further system-model analysis before complete Function coverage can be claimed.
revisit_when: An adopted change alters a skill's public purpose, canonical name, source contract, or output scope.
Specialist analysis establishes additional coherent Functions or explicit REM adoption, or qualified runtime evidence changes a proposed correspondence.

proposed.choice: Replace proposal/proposal-review and combined design with requirement-analysis/requirement-review, system-design and architecture-design.
proposed.rationale: Three distinct authoring responsibilities and one integrated Design Review realize the accepted requirement basis through existing Functions, not one Module per skill.
alternatives: Create one Module and one mandatory review per method.
consequences: Reconcile route, plan, delivery-review, implement, code-review and verify plus conditional resources, examples and templates as one coherent inventory.
Keep methods canonical in rem/; distribute generated versioned resources for selective loading rather than independently maintaining duplicate manuals.
Proposed names are target entrypoints, not additions to the observed public catalog.
The successor MOD-010/011 contracts define proposed v2/v4 operations and capability checks. Skills must not invoke them before actual implementation and adapter availability.

Skills consume supported public task schemas, opaque revisions and code/status/committed outcomes. They supply actor-owned meaning, reread after conflict or uncertain response, and never use raw SQL, table names or runtime coordination files. Saving an assessment neither conducts review nor completes the Change.
revisit_when: Detailed skill contracts or reviewed method ownership require a different entrypoint boundary.
